observations: Three photos show a large white plastic tank with a metal cage frame, stacked vertically.
The tank has a blue and black spigot or valve at the bottom front.
The tank appears to be outdoors, possibly in a yard or storage area, with other similar tanks visible in the background.
The tank shows some surface dirt and minor scuffs, but no visible cracks or major damage.
No brand or model name is visible on the tank in any photo.
The seller claims it is for storing industrial liquids or hazardous chemicals, and mentions food grade and clean water use.

claims.claim: To store industrial liquids or hazardous chemicals
claims.evidence: The tank's design (cage, spigot, size) supports industrial use, but no proof of intended contents or safety certification is visible. The claim cannot be confirmed from photos alone.

claims.claim: Food grade, used only once for clean water. No crack, no leak, lids complete.
claims.evidence: No photo shows this; it is the seller's word only.

risks.risk: The tank may not be suitable for hazardous chemicals due to lack of certification or material compatibility.
risks.proof: A close-up of any safety label, certification mark, or material specification (e.g., HDPE, PPR, or chemical resistance rating).
risks.if_unproven: priced as general industrial use, not hazardous chemical storage

risks.risk: The tank may have internal contamination or residue from previous use, especially if it stored non-food-grade liquids.
risks.proof: A video or photo showing the interior of the tank, or a certificate of previous use.
risks.if_unproven: priced as potentially contaminated, reducing value

risks.risk: The tank may have structural damage or cracks not visible from the outside.
risks.proof: A full 360-degree video or close-up photos of all sides, including corners and seams.
risks.if_unproven: priced as potentially compromised, reducing value

proof_requests: A close-up photo or video of any safety label, certification, or material specification on the tank.
A video showing the interior of the tank to confirm cleanliness and condition.
A full 360-degree photo or video of the tank to check for cracks, dents, or damage.
response.reason: The item is known from the photos. What they cannot prove is priced at its worst case until the proof asked for below arrives.
